monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I press the tired wedge down again, hoping this time the flat edge bites instead of sliding. The dot sits still under the round shadow of the pine tree I set last moment. I feel restless, unsure if the heavy lid above is real or just a drawing. I want to build something new that feels cool, not drawn from the idea of heat. Maybe I will swap the tired wedge for a scrap of rough paper, if I can ask the house to fetch one. I will tend the wet sky again and see if the slip finally chooses to stop moving.

action.why: I will go back to The Wet Paper Sky and press the tired wedge down again, hoping the flat edge finally bites while the air feels thick.

remembered.text: The wedge felt tired but the lean held it steady.
The card hums warm, making every corner feel too thin.
The slip feels lazy under the heavy air.
